take_homes: Start with one agent. Split only for different access, different dialect or different stance.
Give the synthesizer a framework, such as Rumelt's kernel, so it picks a diagnosis and does not average views. I could use this for a leadership team discussion.
Handoffs are where things get lost, and nothing in this module checks whether the result is true.

monday.move: Ask my head of HR operations which recurring people workflow could become one agent, and write down what data it would need to see, for the DPO.
monday.who: Me and one HR business partner
monday.stop_condition: The workflow needs employee-level data, or the DPO and works council have not been asked.
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and I have not asked yet.

misconception.why: The module never talks about roles, headcount or who does this work now. The split-by-access idea made me think about data governance, but I still believe the question is which roles go.

one_line: Good rule for when to use several agents, but it was all about the tool and nobody said what it means for the people doing the work today.
